hints: Integrate the derivative $\frac{dy}{dx} = 3(4x - 7)^{1/2} - 4x^{-1/2}$ term by term with respect to $x$.
Use the reverse chain rule for the first term: $\int 3(4x - 7)^{1/2} dx = \frac{3(4x - 7)^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2} \times 4} = \frac{1}{2}(4x - 7)^{3/2}$.
Integrate $-4x^{-1/2}$ to $-8x^{1/2}$ and include the constant of integration $+c$.
Substitute the coordinates of the given point $\left(4, \frac{5}{2}\right)$ to determine $c$.
walkthrough:
Integrate $\frac{dy}{dx}$ term by term with respect to $x$:
$$y = \int \left(3(4x - 7)^{1/2} - 4x^{-1/2}\right) dx$$
$$y = \frac{3(4x - 7)^{3/2}}{\frac{3}{2} \times 4} - \frac{4x^{1/2}}{\frac{1}{2}} + c = \frac{1}{2}(4x - 7)^{3/2} - 8x^{1/2} + c$$

Substitute the given point $\left(4, \frac{5}{2}\right)$ into the integrated expression to find $c$:
$$\frac{5}{2} = \frac{1}{2}(4(4) - 7)^{3/2} - 8(4)^{1/2} + c$$
$$\frac{5}{2} = \frac{1}{2}(9)^{3/2} - 8(2) + c = \frac{1}{2}(27) - 16 + c = \frac{27}{2} - 16 + c = -\frac{5}{2} + c$$
$$c = \frac{5}{2} + \frac{5}{2} = 5$$

State the final equation of the curve:
$$y = \frac{1}{2}(4x - 7)^{3/2} - 8x^{1/2} + 5$$
